title: Domestication of the horse
summary: A genetic study traced modern domestic horses to the Volga-Don region, where they were domesticated around 2200 BCE. Two genetic differences stand out: one linked to more docile behaviour and one to a stronger backbone. From about 2000 BCE these horses spread rapidly across Eurasia alongside spoke-wheeled chariots, and replaced almost all other local horse populations.

uncertainty.note: Librado et al. (2021) demonstrate from 273 ancient genomes that modern domestic horses (DOM2 lineage) originated in the Volga-Don region c. 2200 BCE and expanded rapidly across Eurasia by 2000 BCE; CNRS dates the initial domestication in the northern Caucasus to around 2200 years BCE.

where.modern_name: Lower Volga-Don region; stand-in pin at Volgograd, Russia
where.historical_name: Western Eurasian steppe between the lower Don and Volga rivers, northern Caucasus periphery (Middle to Late Bronze Age; no recorded polity)

importance.justification: The domestication and Eurasian dispersal of modern domestic horses remade land transportation, pastoral economies, and cavalry warfare across continents for four millennia.

related.because: The rapid expansion of domestic DOM2 horses alongside spoke-wheeled chariots from c. 2000 BCE facilitated the mobility of Indo-Iranian and other steppe pastoralist populations into Central and South Asia.
